blocker.summary: r436 root-caused r435's SIGSEGV to a null global object pointer at guest address 0x82935D98 that sub_821D6C20 dispatches through. r437 pushed further: armed a hardware watchpoint on that address's host mapping from immediately after GuestAddressSpace construction (i.e. before any guest code runs, confirmed via the real base_ member value 0x00007ffef5800000 read off a real symbol breakpoint) through to the crash. The watchpoint never fired -- proof, not inference, that no code (guest or host) writes this address anywhere during the entire observed run, from the very first instruction to the SIGSEGV. This rules out an execution-order side effect of r413/r422/r430; there is simply no writer exercised at all. Attempted to find the writer statically via Ghidra headless (the repo's own .tools/ is empty, but a sibling workspace's ghidra_12.1.2_PUBLIC install was reused read-only against this repo's own ghidra-projects/ace-combat-6 project, verified to point at this repo's own game-files/default.xex): FindReferencesToRange.java and FindPpcSplitAddressMaterialization.java both returned zero hits, and DumpFunction.java showed sub_821D6C20 has never been disassembled or defined as a function in this stored Ghidra project at all -- consistent with it never having been individually studied before (it was unreachable before this session's fix chain). A full/targeted Ghidra re-analysis of that region was not attempted this cycle (potentially costly, changes stored project state, judged not to decide unilaterally). Two hypotheses remain undistinguished: a missing host stub for an unmodeled Xbox 360 subsystem, or a legitimate environment-dependent conditional that correctly skips construction offline but leaves sub_821D6C20 unable to cope. Named for r438, two independent tracks: (1) if the user accepts the cost, run a targeted Ghidra auto-analysis of the sub_821D6C20/0x82935D98 region to enable a real static search; (2) in parallel, resume the unrelated open thread from r434/r435 (PinnedShaderRuntime's 64 MiB shared-memory window), since that affects a different function on a different execution path (VdSwap service, not the entry thread). No source touched this cycle; gates/ctest unaffected. The wider native/ backlog commit decision (r433) remains open, unrelated.
